title: docs(fields): compile the README's snippets against the shipped surface (objectui#5174 batch 36)

**The ledger row's wording was stale** — it said "2 undefined-name diagnostic(s) ... 1 unresolved-module diagnostic(s)". The unresolved-module half is accurate (TS2307 x1); the "undefined-name" half is not: the live codes are TS7031 (implicit any on a destructured binding), not TS2304/TS2552, and nothing on this page "continues an earlier block". Carry-forward from batch 35 confirmed a sixth time: **a ledger row's wording is not evidence.**

## Negative control — the base page had NO passing fence, so the usual subject did not exist

The brief's negative control asks whether the PASSING fences were bound or unbound. Reading 1 has zero passing fences, so that question has no subject here. Instead the same length-preserving decimal technique was pointed at the FAILING blocks, to measure how much of each was checked at all. Run on the tracked file with the trap/restore discipline below (HEAD already carried the repairs, so a restore point existed).

| leg | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| A control | base page verbatim | reproduces reading 1 exactly: 3 diagnostics, same codes, blob `c0748e9aa` |
| B | base + `field.type` -> `field.typo` | **no new diagnostic** — 3, unchanged |
| C | base + `'color'` -> `1234567` (7 chars for 7, 52-byte line for 52) | **4 diagnostics** — a new `TS2345 Argument of type 'number' is not assignable to parameter of type 'string'` |

**Reading: the base page was HALF bound.** The TS7031 block was fully unbound — `field` was implicit `any`, so every member name written on it (`field.type`) was checked by nothing; the page could have documented any spelling at all. The TS2307 block kept its ARGUMENT positions checked despite the failed import, so `registerFieldRenderer`'s `string` parameter was live even while the block was red. Leg B is the one that makes the repair worth its diff: `field.type` was decoration, and is now a checked member access (positive-control leg M5).

## The repairs

**Fence 25 (registration).** The relative import of a file that does not exist becomes a typed stand-in: `declare const MyCustomColorPicker` annotated with React's `FC` generic instantiated at `CellRendererProps` (batch 35's fence-161 precedent), with `CellRendererProps` imported from `@object-ui/fields` and `FC` type-imported from `react`. `registerFieldRenderer('color', MyCustomColorPicker)` is unchanged.

**Teaching point, corrected.** The old comment read `// Register a new 'color' field type`. `color` is SHIPPED twice over — `standardMap.color = ColorSwatchCellRenderer` (`packages/fields/src/index.tsx:2385`), the `ColorField` widget in `fieldWidgetMap` (`:2801`), and `ColorFieldMetadata` in `@object-ui/types` — and `getCellRenderer` consults the registry BEFORE the standard map (`:2322` then `:2384`). So the call OVERRIDES a shipped renderer; it does not add a type. The comment now says exactly that, and points at the way to ADD one (register a name nothing ships).

**Fence 37 -> 42 (grid cell).** `({ field, value })` is annotated `CellRendererProps` — the real props bag, not a narrowed stand-in. `field.type` then type-checks against the 37-member `FieldMetadata` union (`packages/types/src/field-types.ts:824`), whose every member declares `type`; `getCellRenderer` takes `string`, so the union of literals is assignable. No widening was needed and none was added.

**Phantom keys authored by the fences: none.** Control leg M3 proves the bound is real: `CellRendererProps` carries no index signature, so an invented prop is refused.

**Prose claims verified against the sources (step 6):**
- "You can override standard fields or add new ones" — **TRUE**, and now the snippet demonstrates the override half honestly (registry first at `:2322`, standard map second).
- "View components use `getCellRenderer` to resolve the correct component for a field type" — **TRUE**, verified at five shipped sites: `plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx:601`, `plugin-detail/src/RelatedList.tsx:936`, `DetailSection.tsx:296`, `HeaderHighlight.tsx:134`, `RecordMetaFooter.tsx:105`.
- Two claims did NOT hold up and are filed rather than fixed here (out of this batch's surface): the feature bullet's `FieldRegistry` names a symbol nothing exports (#8292), and the fence's raw `getCellRenderer(field.type)` skips the `resolveCellRendererType` step every shipped consumer performs (#8294).

## Four-axis reasoning on the two real choices

**1. Reword the comment vs. register a genuinely unused type name.**
- *Real business need*: measured — `color` is shipped at three sites, and the section's own heading promises BOTH paths ("override standard fields or add new ones"). The page had no example of the override path; renaming the type would have left the override path undocumented and the shipped precedence rule unstated.
- *Long-term soundness*: the precedence (`registry` before `standardMap`) is the durable fact a reader needs; naming an arbitrary unused type teaches nothing about it and rots the day someone ships that name.
- *Anti-AI-error* (deciding axis): "Register a new 'color' field type" is exactly the sentence that makes an AI silently REPLACE a shipped renderer while believing it added one. Naming the override, in the block that performs it, is the structural fix.
- *Startup focus*: zero new surface — one comment, no new example, no new API.

**2. `CellRendererProps` vs. a `Pick` of it over `field` and `value`.**
- *Real business need*: the cell forwards the props bag straight into the resolved renderer, which requires the full `CellRendererProps`; a `Pick` would describe a shape nothing in the codebase constructs.
- *Long-term soundness*: one name, the shipped one, so the doc moves when the interface moves.
- *Anti-AI-error*: `Pick` would teach that a cell may drop `isEditing`/`onChange` — both are optional today, so a `Pick` is indistinguishable at the type level while being false about the contract. Naming the real interface keeps the doc honest if either becomes required.
- *Startup focus*: no new type alias to maintain.

Reported deviation from the brief: the brief's suggested control leg (swapping `field` and `value`) cannot go red — `value` is `any`, so the swap type-checks. Legs M1/M2 measure that boundary directly instead, and M5/M6 were added to cover the two things the repair actually buys.
